argumentsFor: It provides the RBI a flexible, market-based instrument to manage short-term liquidity.
A one-day tenor allows temporary absorption without creating a lasting tightening commitment.
The variable-rate format enables market-determined bidding rather than a wholly fixed administered rate.
background: Under a reverse repo operation, banks place funds with the RBI against eligible collateral and receive interest; liquidity moves from the banking system to the central bank for the operation’s tenor.

officialFacts.text: On a review of current and evolving liquidity conditions, it has been decided to conduct a Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction on Thursday, November 19, 2026.
The auction window is 10:30 AM to 11:00 AM.
The date of reversal is November 20, 2026 (Friday).
The operational guidelines for the auction as given in the Reserve Bank’s Press Release 2019-2020/1947 dated February 13, 2020 will remain the same.

example.heading: Hypothetical illustration
example.text: Illustration: If banks temporarily have more deployable funds than needed in the overnight market, a one-day VRRR auction could allow them to place some funds with the RBI and receive them back on the notified reversal date. This is only an illustration of the mechanism, not a reported event.

pocketRead.excerpt: The RBI will absorb ₹50,000 crore through a one-day VRRR auction on 19 November 2026, with bidding from 10:30–11:00 AM and reversal on 20 November.

question.answer: The auction absorbs liquidity temporarily: banks bid to place funds with the RBI for one day, reducing funds available in the market during that period; reversal restores the funds on 20 November. Its variable-rate design allows bidding to determine the accepted rate, while the source does not establish the auction’s final outcome.

sections.heading: The notified operation
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank announced on 18 November 2026 that it would conduct a VRRR auction under the LAF on Thursday, 19 November. The notified amount is ₹50,000 crore, the tenor is one day, the auction window is 10:30 AM to 11:00 AM, and reversal is scheduled for Friday, 20 November.
The RBI said the decision followed a review of current and evolving liquidity conditions and that the operational guidelines in its 13 February 2020 press release would remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Mechanism and reading the signal
paragraphs: In a VRRR operation, participating banks can place funds with the RBI for the notified tenor through an auction. This temporarily absorbs liquidity and returns it on the reversal date, making the operation reversible rather than a permanent withdrawal.

The announcement indicates an operational liquidity-management action, but by itself it does not prove a change in the policy rate or establish the exact cause of liquidity conditions. The source also does not report the auction’s realised absorption or outcome.

advisory_notes: The static definition and background correctly explain the usual VRRR mechanism, but the supplied press release itself does not reproduce the referenced operational guidelines.

“Eligible participants” and collateral details are plausible mechanism-level background, not established by the supplied extract; retain them only as general analysis or verify from the 13 February 2020 guidelines.
“Variable-rate format enables market-determined bidding” is broadly accurate, but the accepted rate and realised absorption are not reported for this auction.
The phrase “RBI will absorb ₹50,000 crore” in the pocketRead headline and deck overstates the announcement: ₹50,000 crore is the notified amount, not the confirmed realised absorption.
The claim that funds are “returned” on the reversal date is a reasonable description of a completed operation, but this extract only schedules reversal and does not report completion.
The anchor GS3.1 and the monetary-policy/liquidity-management connection are substantively relevant; however, the proposed code is an editorial taxonomy rather than an official UPSC syllabus label.
“Align money-market conditions with the RBI’s operating framework” and “preserves flexibility” are analytical implications, not conclusions demonstrated by this single announcement.

wayForward: Use VRRR in conjunction with broader liquidity monitoring rather than infer a policy stance from a single auction.
Communicate the notified amount, tenor, window and reversal date clearly to support predictable money-market operations.
Assess realised bids and liquidity conditions before drawing conclusions about transmission or stance; those outcomes are not supplied in the record.
